title: Adjunction-normalized augmented Cech model after derived pushforward
statement:
Let $\mathcal X,\mathcal V$ be topoi on small sites in the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings and Grothendieck abelian module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Let $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal V$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] with exact module inverse image. Let $v:V\to1_{\mathcal X}$ be an epimorphism of sheaves of sets, let $v_n:\mathcal X/(V^{\times(n+1)})\to\mathcal X$ be the slice localizations with pulled-back rings [def-pur-localized-ringed-site, def-sfb-element-site-localization], and let $N$ be a module sheaf on $\mathcal X$. Use the actual localization adjunctions, their restriction maps and units, as in [def-sfb-coherent-cech-image-model]. Write $N_n=v_n^*N$ and use ordinary K-injective derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. There is a coherent nonnegative cosimplicial complex $B^{n,\bullet}$ of modules on $\mathcal V$, together with column isomorphisms and an augmented-total isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal V))$,
$$\beta_n:QB^{n,\bullet}\xrightarrow{\sim}C_n:=R(fv_n)_*(N_n[0]),\qquad \alpha:Rf_*(N[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}QT(B).$$
Here $Q$ localizes complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, $T(B)^r=\bigoplus_{n+q=r}B^{n,q}$, and the differential is $\delta+(-1)^n d$, where $\delta$ is the alternating coface differential [def-sp-double-complex-total]. All indices and any added resolution degrees are nonnegative. The isomorphisms $\beta_n$ use the canonical adjunction-normalized comparisons $Rf_*Rv_{n*}\cong R(fv_n)_*$ of [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] (for the exact left adjoints $f^*$ and $v_n^*$) and identify all cofaces and codegeneracies with the actual Cech restriction maps. The augmentation $\alpha$ is the derived restriction augmentation; its degree-zero column is $Rf_*$ of the localization unit $N[0]\to Rv_{0*}v_0^*(N[0])$, whose degree-zero sheaf map is restriction of sections. These comparisons and augmentations are natural in module maps $N\to N'$ and covering refinements $W\to V$ over $1_{\mathcal X}$ between epimorphic covers, as maps of entire coherent augmented models, independently of compatible resolution choices. No Cartesian coefficient identification for $f$ is required beyond exactness of its module inverse image.

proof.text: Apply the column-model theorem only to the identity ringed morphism. This supplies injective resolutions, coherent image models, and K-injective restricted resolutions with their quasi-isomorphic restriction maps. Slice module categories have K-injective resolutions by the small-site Grothendieck theorem.

Reuse the existing strict diagram B and augmentation of the column model: in degree n its complex is the n-th column of the coherent bicomplex, and every operator is the actual image restriction followed by f.modules. Naturality of the image functor gives the complex and cosimplicial equations. Its alternating-coface bicomplex is identified with the existing coherent bicomplex by component identities; the equality of differentials is additivity of f.modules. Applying totalFunctor gives totalIso, fixed on every diagonal inclusion.

Apply the generalized exact image-augmentation theorem directly to f. Its existing sectionwise proof does not require a Cartesian ring-map assumption. It gives a normalized b that is a quasi-isomorphism. The canonical resolution comparison is an isomorphism, so alpha followed by Q(totalIso.inv) is an isomorphism. This avoids the separate finite-total derived comparison.

For each column, use the extension/map comparison and imageIso for its termwise representative. Its restricted injective resolution is K-injective. The right-derived unit on this resolution is invertible; compose it with the inverse of the right-derived image of its restriction quasi-isomorphism. Transport the localized strict cosimplicial diagram along these column isomorphisms. Their definition proves the column-unit equation. The exact localization left adjoint implies that D.push preserves K-injectives; use the canonical right-derived composition isomorphism. Its universal-unit factorization, transported from the homotopy category through quotientCompQhIso, proves the displayed composite-unit equation for every complex. This is the same source comparison used in the adjunction-normalization theorem: its universal-unit equation uniquely fixes the comparison.

Lift module maps between injective resolutions. Reuse the existing private augmentation and resolution-comparison naturality lemmas via import all to obtain the total alpha square. The existing refinement laws give the refinement square, identities and composition. Any two lifts are homotopic; apply the existing signed-total lift-independence theorem, and map the same homotopy through each additive column functor. Construct coherent maps between arbitrary column presentations by conjugating the canonical strict map with the presentation natural isomorphisms. Restriction-unit naturality proves their augmentation square.

The functor and refinement laws give identity and composition of both total and column transitions. The existing resolution-comparison law gives localized total isomorphisms. A reverse resolution lift is inverse on each localized column because both composites are homotopic to identities.
